GEO.fp_notes: Distinctive prefix. GSE/GSM/GPL/GDS covered by one namespace. Rarely collides in prose.

SRA.source: identifiers.org:insdc.sra (tightened: \d+ -> \d{6,}; real SRA accessions are 6+ digits)
SRA.fp_notes: Covers SRR/SRX/SRP/SRS/SRA/SRZ + ERR/ERX/ERP/ERS + DRR/DRX/DRP/DRS. identifiers.org allows any digit count; 6-digit minimum removes short false hits like 'ERP123'.

BioSample.fp_notes: SAMN (NCBI), SAMEA (EBI), SAMD (DDBJ). Optional letter handles SAMEA.

GenBank_ENA_DDBJ.fp_notes: Letter+digit shapes collide heavily with grant numbers (e.g. 'Y21026'), museum specimen codes, catalogue numbers, cell-line names. Rod Page found ~49% of a sampled 1,000 corpus 'GenBank' accessions unknown to GenBank. Require context cue (GenBank/ENA/DDBJ/accession nearby) or validate against ENA/NCBI. SRA run/study/sample shapes ([SED]R[APRSXZ]\d{6,}) were added 2026-09-03: they are unambiguous, do not collide with any of the FP shapes above (verified: the change newly accepts only SRA-shaped strings), and excluding them silently dropped 143,933 citations as regex_invalid -- including ones the repository-evidence tier (sql/66-68) is built to decide, since it filters FOR SRA shapes and sra_bq_metadata exists for exactly that.

PDB.fp_notes: Digit + 3 alphanumerics matches '24hr', '2019', '1000', figure labels, mouse-line codes. Rod Page: 18% of corpus PDB IDs failed even this format; only ~71% of the rest existed in PDB. Only accept with a 'PDB' context cue and/or existence check; consider requiring at least one letter. New extended format pdb_XXXXXXXX not covered.

UniProt.source: identifiers.org:uniprot (cleaned: the registry pattern literally contains commas/spaces inside character classes, e.g. '[A-Z, 0-9]', and an unanchored alternation; this is the corrected strict form of the official UniProt regex)
UniProt.fp_notes: 6-char accessions (P12345, Q9Y6K1) can collide with product codes and other short alphanumerics. 10-char A0A... accessions are distinctive.

Ensembl.source: identifiers.org:ensembl (stricter: the registry pattern ends with a catch-all alternative '[A-Z_a-z0-9]+(\.)?(t)?(\d+)?([a-z])?' that matches almost any token; this form keeps only the ENS-stable-ID shape incl. species infixes like ENSMUSG)
Ensembl.fp_notes: ENS prefix + 11 digits is highly distinctive. Non-ENS Ensembl IDs (FlyBase FBgn..., yeast systematic names) deliberately not covered here.

ArrayExpress.source: identifiers.org:arrayexpress (stricter: registry '^[AEP]-\w{4}-\d+$' also matches array designs A-* and protocols P-*, and \w permits lowercase/underscore; experiments E-XXXX-n are what get cited as data)
ArrayExpress.fp_notes: E-MTAB, E-GEOD, E-MEXP, E-PROT etc. Distinctive shape.

PRIDE.source: identifiers.org:px (stricter: registry allows optional 'R' prefix for reprocessed RPXD datasets; drop it for citation mining)

MetaboLights.source: identifiers.org:metabolights (stricter: registry '^MTBL[CS]\d+$' also matches MTBLC compound records, which are reference entries, not study deposits)

Pfam.fp_notes: Short prefix; 'PF' + digits occurs in product/part codes. Usually cited with 'Pfam' nearby.

dbGaP.source: identifiers.org:dbgap (stricter: registry leaves the dots unescaped, '(.v\d+.p\d+)?')
dbGaP.fp_notes: Lowercase 'phs' + 6 digits is distinctive; keep case-sensitive.

EMDB.fp_notes: Collides with Merck compound codes (e.g. EMD-121974/cilengitide have 6 digits, but 4-5 digit EMD compound codes exist in older pharmacology literature). Context cue 'EMDB' or 'cryo-EM' helps.

Cellosaurus.source: identifiers.org:cellosaurus (stricter: registry appends an artifact '(\.txt)?' suffix)
Cellosaurus.fp_notes: Distinctive prefix. Note: cites a cell line (a research resource), not a dataset deposit.

dbSNP.fp_notes: Extremely common token shape; rsIDs are gene-variant references, not dataset citations. Several top Kaggle solutions excluded rs* entirely. Keep case-sensitive lowercase 'rs'.

GISAID.source: convention (no identifiers.org namespace found for GISAID isolates; pattern matches EuropePMC/Kaggle usage)
GISAID.fp_notes: Distinctive prefix. GISAID also uses EPI\d+ segment IDs and EPI_SET_ dataset IDs, not covered here.

TCIA.source: convention (TCIA has no accession scheme; collections are cited via DOIs under prefix 10.7937; no identifiers.org namespace found)
TCIA.fp_notes: DOI-shaped; route through the DOI pipeline rather than accession matching.

Dryad.source: convention (Dryad IDs are DOIs under prefix 10.5061; the legacy 'doi:10.5061/dryad.xxxx' suffix form is the only non-URL variant seen in text)
Dryad.fp_notes: DOI-shaped; route through the DOI pipeline. Bare 'dryad.8515' occasionally appears in older articles.

EGA_study.fp_notes: Distinctive shape, but note: the 1st-place Kaggle team excluded EGA as false-positive-prone / low-yield in the competition data.

GCA_assembly.source: identifiers.org:insdc.gca (GCA_ only there: ^GCA_[0-9]{9}(\.[0-9]+)?$; GCF_ RefSeq assemblies added by analogy)
GCA_assembly.fp_notes: Format itself is distinctive, but genome-assembly accessions overwhelmingly denote reuse of reference genomes, not new data; top Kaggle solutions excluded GCA_* as false-positive-prone for 'primary data citation'.
